children: Kuwait International Bank has raised $500 million from a five-year benchmark-sized sukuk priced at par, with a 5.502% fixed-rate coupon paid semi-annually.
The wakala and murabaha issuance has a 5.502% yield, with a reoffer spread of T+95bps.
IPTs for the senior unsecured sukuk were in the T+125bps area.
The final orderbook was in excess of $1 billion, excluding JLM interest.
The Kuwait lender is listed as the obligor, with KIB Sukuk Limited named issuer. The sukuk has an expected rating of A by Fitch, in line with KIB’s own rating.
The sukuk has an issue date of September 10, 2026, with a 2031 maturity, with a listing on the London Stock Exchange’s International Securities Market.
The issuance will come under KIB Sukuk Limited’s $1.5 billion Trust Certificate Issuance Programme, a special purpose vehicle incorporated in the Cayman Islands.

Citi and Standard Chartered are the banks mandated as joint global coordinators, together with Arab Bank, ASB Capital, Bank ABC, Boubyan Bank, Emirates NBD Capital, KFH Capital, KIB Invest, QNB Capital, Sharjah Islamic Bank and Warba Bank as joint lead managers and bookrunners. Citi is also listed as the billing and delivery bank.

KIB’s sukuk is one of several DCM issuances by GCC-based banks this week, including the Saudi-based Arab National Bank’s $750 million AT1 and the Jeddah-headquartered Islamic Development Bank’s $1.5 billon debt raise. A Saudi sovereign issuance also made it to the markets, raising $3.25 billion on Tuesday through a dual-tranche bond.
(Writing by Bindu Rai, editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Kuwait International Bank raises $500mln with 5-year benchmark sukuk
